memories.content: Specify a single representative measure that serves as the criterion for retaining, modifying, or discarding compared design alternatives.
HCI review panels verify whether clear criteria for judging design alternatives are established using the declared primary measure.
Collect process measures to diagnose interaction steps where problems occurred, alongside the primary outcome measure.
Interpret evaluation results as differences between compared design alternatives rather than as success or failure of a single prototype.
Check boundary cases to verify whether the derived design principles retain explanatory power for adjacent situations not included in the comparison.
Controlled evaluation environments do not reproduce time pressure, peer intervention, or voluntary termination conditions found in daily use.
Specify field and user data sources and analysis procedures corresponding to all HCI research questions.
In preregistered studies, clarify the criteria for judging plan changes.
In preregistered studies, clarify the location for recording plan changes.
Use a justified minimum-to-maximum target range when confirmations can change, and tie the minimum and maximum to different workload and budget cases.
Specify the observation records, system logs, or interview tools used to collect each type of field and user data.
Specify whether each type of field and user data will be collected before, during, or after deployment.
Readers cannot assess a target range unless both bounds have a stated consequence for schedule, workload, or cost.
In field deployments, network and service instability exist as independent causes of task failure alongside design choices.
If a safety signal occurs in the field system, existing institutional safety procedures take precedence over the research schedule and data collection plan.
Reviewers judge answerability by tracing the path from each research question to its data sources and analysis procedures.
The user authoring this proposal tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.
Define what can still be completed at the minimum target instead of treating every number inside the range as operationally identical.
Use a bounded range to absorb expected confirmation changes without pretending that one early estimate is guaranteed.
Show how session count and facilitator time change at the minimum and maximum bounds.
Define the additional workload or deliverable enabled at the maximum target so the upper bound is not an arbitrary cushion.
A bounded range preserves uncertainty honestly but makes the final workload and budget less certain than one fixed target.

analysis.overview: The frames emphasize different parts of HCI evaluation planning. Reference centers comparative design judgment, diagnostic measures, interpretation, transfer, and controlled-setting limits; Compared centers research traceability, preregistration, bounded resource targets, field contingencies, safety precedence, and an authoring tendency. Their environmental cautions are complementary but explicitly setting-dependent.

relations.reason: Both Reference memories split one underlying one-sided policy: establish the decision criterion through a primary measure and have review panels verify that criterion.
relations.summary: A declared primary measure should govern decisions among design alternatives and provide a clear criterion for review.

relations.reason: This diagnostic measurement requirement appears only in Reference and is independently useful from its primary-measure governance policy.
relations.summary: Process measures should accompany the primary outcome measure to locate problematic interaction steps.

relations.reason: This interpretation rule appears only in Reference and governs a separate analytical decision.
relations.summary: Evaluation findings should be interpreted comparatively across alternatives, not as pass-or-fail judgments about one prototype.

relations.reason: This transferability check appears only in Reference and is independent of measurement and result-interpretation policies.
relations.summary: Adjacent boundary cases should test whether derived design principles retain explanatory power beyond the original comparison.

relations.reason: The explicit controlled-versus-field conditions explain and preserve the difference; the claims complement rather than contradict one another under their respective settings.
relations.summary: Evaluation-setting conditions constrain causal interpretation: controlled settings omit everyday pressures, while field settings add infrastructure-related failure causes.

relations.reason: These Compared memories split one planning claim across source and analysis mapping, collection tools, collection timing, and reviewer assessment of the resulting trace.
relations.summary: Field and user research plans should make each question traceable to data sources, collection arrangements, and analysis procedures so answerability can be reviewed.

relations.reason: The two Compared memories split one change-control requirement into decision criteria and documentation location.
relations.summary: Preregistered studies should specify how plan changes are judged and where they are recorded.

relations.reason: These Compared memories jointly elaborate one bounded-range policy through its rationale, minimum and maximum meanings, staffing effects, assessability requirements, and uncertainty tradeoff.
relations.summary: A variable confirmation target should use justified minimum and maximum bounds with distinct deliverables, workload, schedule, and budget consequences while acknowledging residual uncertainty.

relations.reason: This safety-precedence rule appears only in Compared and is operationally independent of its other field-planning claims.
relations.summary: A field-system safety signal should trigger existing institutional procedures ahead of research scheduling and data collection.

relations.reason: This author-specific framing observation appears only in Compared and is independent of the methodological policies.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to present implemented feature lists directly as design contributions.

reports.compared_only: Compared uniquely covers question-to-method traceability, preregistered change records, consequence-based target ranges, safety overrides, and feature-list framing.
reports.differences: Controlled studies omit everyday pressures, whereas field deployments introduce infrastructure failures independent of design; these cautions apply in different evaluation settings.
reports.reference_only: Reference uniquely defines primary-measure governance, process diagnostics, comparative interpretation, and boundary-case testing.
